title: Query Lens: Interpreting Sparse Key-Value Features with Indirect Effects
claim: Prior lenses read a feature only through its direct effect; ours adds indirect downstream effects to give coherent interpretations.
layout: 2 stacked panels: schematic top, comparison bottom; color-coded vectors summed
description: The top panel (a) is a schematic of the residual stream. Light-blue rounded boxes are connected by a black line, with purple hexagons marking residual updates. A feature vector (1) in a blue box at the lower left, labeled Layer 1 / Index 17000, writes into the stream. Red, blue and brown colored paths run through a pink Stream Transition region (2) into a green Readout region (3), which holds a U^T unembedding trapezoid. A brace below sums the red Direct Effect bar and the blue and brown Indirect Effects bars. The bottom panel (b) compares Logit Lens and Query Lens. Logit Lens turns the red vector into a bar histogram and Top-K tokens that are gibberish, with a red question mark and the label 'Not Interpretable!'. Query Lens sums the red, blue and brown vectors into a purple vector, and Top-K gives coherent tokens (Everest, summit, GoPro) that match the quoted text 'Travel documentary filmmaking across global locations.'
caption: Overview of Query Lens. (a) A feature written into the residual stream is read as a query by downstream modules, producing indirect effects. (b) Logit Lens projects features directly into vocabulary space and misses these indirect effects. Query Lens accounts for them and provides a more faithful interpretation.
abstract: While sparse autoencoders provide features more interpretable than individual neurons, reliably characterizing them remains challenging. We propose Query Lens, which extends Logit Lens to enable more comprehensive and faithful interpretations of sparse features. By jointly considering encoder-side key features and decoder-side value features, we identify both the inputs that activate a feature and the outputs it promotes. We also account for indirect, module-mediated effects that arise when the feature is processed by downstream modules, going beyond the direct effect captured by Logit Lens. In experiments, we find that Query Lens yields coherent token signatures for features that remain uninterpretable under Logit Lens. Finally, we propose the Subspace Channel Hypothesis, suggesting that downstream modules read features through layer-specific subspaces.
